Based on the feedback from the recent rule review/discussion, the modteam wanted to have a follow-up discussion about rule 6 and see if the community would like any adjustments made in how the sub currently handles illegal content. The current language of the rule is below:

  1. No links to illegal torrents or other illegal downloads/content.

This was changed to add the word illegal. This means no cracked games or copyrighted material unfairly distributed.

You can however link to torrents in cases where developers may be distributing their games via this medium (or other software etc)

Links to other content such as abandonware and non-console emulators (such as Apple II or Commodore 64 emulation and roms) are allowed.

/v/gaming's rules belong to the community, so please take part in the discussion and let us know how you would like us to handle illegal content moving forward.

Edit: so far there's been universal support for the rule and a number of great reasons started throughout the thread. We've gotten more feedback than we could have hoped for, so I appreciate everyone who took the time to weigh in and keep /v/gaming's rules in the hands of the community.

@Cynabuns brought up a good point that illegal content is already covered in full by Voat's site-wide user agreement. What would you think of /v/gaming scratching this rule from the sidebar and having mods point to the user agreement when removing links to illegal content?

So for example, I can talk about playing Mario 64 as a ROM using RetroArch, and I can link to RetroArch; I just can't link to the Mario 64 ROM.

This kind of stuff is easy enough to find and it's just easier to not link it, for both Voat and the sub. As long as this is only covering direct piracy and not fan games, bootlegs, and the such, which are all technically illegal but it's just not the same as straight up linking a ROM site.

The only exception I can think of is if there is a ROM linked as part of a bigger story, such as this story on ET for the Atari 2600. It has both the original ROM and the fixed version in the story because they are directly relevant. This is a lot different than straight up linking someone directly to a ROM site and I would hate for people not to be able to link interesting stories because they happen to contain a relevant ROM.
